scenarios.setting: Someone compliments your presentation and you instinctively want to dismiss it.
scenarios.jab: That was a really clear presentation.

replies.line: Thank you. I worked hard on making it clear.
replies.why: It receives the compliment and acknowledges the effort without claiming perfection.
replies.delivery: Pause and smile before “thank you”; avoid adding “but” and a list of flaws.

replies.why: It accepts the praise without arguing or requiring reassurance.
replies.delivery: Pause and smile before “thank you”; avoid adding “but” and a list of flaws.

replies.line: That's kind of you; I'm glad the key points came through.
replies.why: It connects the compliment to the presentation's purpose while expressing gratitude.
replies.delivery: Keep “That's kind of you” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly.

replies.line: Thank you; the rehearsal audience was mostly my houseplant.
replies.why: Self-directed humor accepts the praise while keeping the exchange light.
replies.delivery: Pause and smile before “thank you”; avoid adding “but” and a list of flaws.

followUp.line: Thank you; that means a lot.
followUp.why: It continues receiving the compliment without turning it into a debate.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “Thank you,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
